```text

Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — *"Model tier — no path-derived mandate … the tier stays the PM's per-card judgment call (floor sonnet · default opus · ceiling fable)."* — derived in a detached worktree at `c5d3d1d8b69e`, ⛔ not from the shared checkout, which is stale and would have exited 0 anyway. Judged default judgment tier, ⛔ not the floor: this is the runtime half of a ruling whose spec half already landed, so the work is reading what the OTHER half actually declared and honouring it, ⛔ not inventing a reading.
Clause-②: no
Thread-read: (no comments on the card at claim time)
Serial constraints cleared: nothing in flight in this lane. ⭐ `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` was held by PR #19326 (#19120) earlier today and that has LANDED (`13d52947d8`), so it is free. PR #19391 is armed on `packages/create-objectstack/**` + two root declarations — disjoint.
```

## The job

**Ruling item 2 of #17667.** Items 1, 3 and 4 landed in PR #19364 (squash `ada70122`). Item 2 could not go with them: it lands in `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, which the lane table puts on `domain:cli`, while #17667 is `domain:spec`'s. ⭐ The ruling itself assigned this item to 「the cli seat's sibling PR」 verbatim — this card is that sibling's carrier.

**The spec door now declares an `enabled` query parameter. The runtime door never reads it.**

## ⚠️ Read the landed half FIRST

⛔ Do not derive the semantics from this card's prose. **Read PR #19364 and the spec declaration it landed**, and honour exactly what they say: the parameter's name, its type, its default when absent, and what it is declared to do. ⭐ A runtime door that implements a *plausible* reading of `enabled` rather than the *declared* one recreates the very split this ruling exists to close.

⚠️ In particular, settle from the declaration — ⛔ not by guessing — what happens when the parameter is **absent**, and whether absent and an explicit value are meant to differ.

## What this seat knows about this file, from landing #19120 in it today

PR #19326 landed a `version` gate here. Two things from that round worth carrying:

- the door asks a declared grammar **by reference** (`ManifestSchema.shape.version`), ⛔ never a re-spelled regex. ⭐ Do the same here: read `enabled` off the spec declaration rather than re-describing it.
- ⚠️ that round graded on **one** of five classes the door mishandles, and the other four are filed as **#19328**. ⛔ Do not fix them here. If you touch code adjacent to them, leave them alone and say so.

## Deliverable

The door reads `enabled` as declared, with tests pinning the declared behaviour including the absent case. Your report must say **which declaration you read it from**, quoted.

## Fences

⛔ Never edit `content/docs/releases/`. ⛔ `packages/spec/**` belongs to the spec seat — if the runtime half cannot be implemented without a spec change, **STOP and report**; that is a cross-lane finding, not this round's work. Changeset: derive from the repo's gates; if required, `patch` — ⛔ never `major`. Commit trailers **model-free**: `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` plus a `Claude-Session:` line. English. Draft PR, `Fixes #19394`.

⚠️ If any part of this order is imprecise or contradicts what you measure, **say so and stop rather than silently matching it** — four of this seat's orders were wrong this shift and a dev caught every one.

## Landing record — #19394 is on `main`. Ruling item 2 of #17667 is closed.

PR #19405 merged through the queue at 17:32Z. Verified by **content**, ⛔ not by the merge event.

| leg | reading |
|---|---|
| squash commit | `0862063ba782e86abfe064470b1eb4a4b7ebb4cd` |
| shape | `git rev-list --parents -n 1` = **2 fields** ⇒ squash |
| committed | `2026-09-20T17:04:25Z` — the **enqueue** timestamp |
| parent | `6af29010b9a3` |
| pre-squash head | `9d16b5ab7e` is **NOT** an ancestor of `origin/main` |

### ⚠️ My first control was WRONG, and chasing it found something

I probed `returns every remaining row` expecting **0/1** and measured **1/1**. ⛔ That is a discrepancy, not a pass, so it was chased rather than explained away.

The line was **edited, not removed**:

| | text |
|---|---|
| parent | ``this door applies the `status` / `type` `` … `filters and then returns every remaining row` |
| landing | ``this door applies the `status` / `type` / `` … ```enabled` filters and then returns every remaining row`` |

⇒ my probe picked a substring that **survives the edit**. ⛔ Distinct from #19323's dud (0 on both sides, discriminating nothing) — this one measured an unchanged fragment, which is a *wrong* probe rather than an empty one.

⭐ **And the thing it turned up is better than the control:** the dev proactively corrected the **in-code copy** of exactly the stale enumeration filed as **#19407**.

### Content — corrected two-sided control

| probe | on `0862063ba7` | on the parent `6af29010b9` |
|---|---|---|
| ```enabled` filters and then`` | **1** | 0 |
| ```status` / `type` `` at line end — the old two-filter spelling | 0 | **1** |
| `[#19394]` marker | **2** | 0 |
| `packages-list-enabled-filter.test.ts` exists | **yes** | no |

### What landed

The list branch reads `enabled` as `ListInstalledPackagesRequestSchema` declares it — `enabled: z.boolean().optional()`. Four decisions taken **off that line** rather than invented: absent means **no filter** (no `.default()`, so `undefined` never collapses into `false`); absent and an explicit `false` are **different requests**; the coercion is the repo's **one** parser for a declared `z.boolean()` wire key ⇒ a third spelling is **refused 400**, ⛔ not guessed; and the row side reads the row's own `enabled`, ⛔ not `status`.

### ⭐ The flag that mattered most

The ruling's wording for item 2 is *"one filter line, same shape as `status`"*. The dev implemented to the **declaration** and flagged that **the shape half does not transfer**: `status` is a truthiness guard plus string equality, which on a declared boolean admits the truthy string `'false'` and then matches no row — handing the caller who asked for the disabled half an **empty list on a `200`**.

⇒ following the ruling's prose literally would have produced a **silent wrong answer**. ⭐ Caught by reading the declaration *against* the sentence rather than treating the sentence as the spec.

### Changeset — ⛔ and an order defect of mine

`minor` + `**BREAKING**` + an ADR-0087 marker, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. My order said `patch`. The diff **narrows a published wire accept set** (`?enabled=1` was `200`-with-every-row, now `400`), and the launch-window convention ships breaking as `minor`. Recorded as order defect #5 at seat-post `5751170079` — ⚠️ the precedent was PR #19326's changeset, **which this seat landed earlier the same day**.

### Docs — a clean negative with a lit control

Nine hand-written pages were anchored to this diff. **None falsified.** The decisive probe: repo-wide `enabled=(1|0|true|false|…)` across `content/docs/` → **0 hits**. ⭐ The lit control: `keepData` → **found**, and one hit is on one of the nine ⇒ the instrument *does* find a documented `/packages` query parameter when one exists, so the zero is an absence it could have seen.

⚠️ And the direction nobody expected: `content/docs/references/api/package-api.mdx:404` has been **publishing `enabled` as a working filter all along while the door ignored it**. ⇒ this diff **repairs** that page rather than falsifying it.

`pm:dispatched` stripped and the assignee cleared in one write, read back.
